title: 13 Best On-Demand Webinar Platforms for B2B Event Teams | Zuddl Blog
summary: Compare 13 on-demand webinar platforms for B2B event teams in 2026 on broadcast modes, CRM sync depth, and content repurposing. Covers strengths, gaps, pricing, and best-fit scenarios.
body_markdown:
‍


Your webinar ended two hours ago. A prospect clicks the registration link from a LinkedIn post your team promoted all week. They land on a page that says "This event has ended." No replay. No form. No way to watch. That lead is gone, and your team will never know they existed.


On-demand webinar platforms manage more than replay hosting. They govern the transition from live broadcast to persistent content asset, control who accesses recordings and under what conditions, sync engagement data into CRM for lead scoring, and determine whether a single webinar generates pipeline for a day or for six months. The operational surface extends from registration through gating, repurposing, and attribution.


This article evaluates 13 platforms across broadcast mode flexibility (live, simulive, and on-demand), CRM sync depth, and content repurposing capability. Each entry covers verified strengths, documented gaps, pricing, and the specific team situation where the tool fits best.

## The 13 best on-demand webinar platforms for B2B event teams


### Zuddl


Zuddl is an AI-native unified events platform that handles live, simulive, and on-demand webinars within a single workflow, with automated transitions between modes. It serves B2B marketing and demand generation teams running recurring webinar programs that need CRM-integrated engagement data and branded post-event content.


**What it does well**


- A single on-demand toggle automatically unpublishes the registration page and publishes the on-demand page at the same URL when the webinar ends, eliminating manual page swaps and preventing late registrants from hitting a dead screen.
- Simulive functionality lets teams blend pre-recorded content with[live Q&A](https://www.zuddl.com/platform/virtual-and-hybrid-events/video-production-and-streaming) , so speakers do not need to present the same session across multiple time zones.
- [Real-time, bi-directional CRM sync](https://www.zuddl.com/event-integrations) with Salesforce, HubSpot, Marketo, Eloqua, and Iterable passes granular engagement data (poll responses, Q&A questions, CTA clicks, minutes watched) into CRM records for lead scoring.
- A[content hub](https://www.zuddl.com/platform/virtual-and-hybrid-events/ai-content-hub) auto-generates highlight reels, short clips, blog drafts, and social posts from webinar recordings, with attendance heatmaps identifying which segments drove the highest engagement.
- [Embedded CTA banners and downloadable resources](https://www.zuddl.com/platform/virtual-and-hybrid-events/event-engagement) appear inside webinars during live and simulive sessions, with CTA clicks indicating buying stage for immediate sales routing via instant Slack notifications that include Salesforce lead fields.


**Where it has gaps**


- Pricing is not publicly listed and requires a sales conversation, which makes initial budget assessment difficult for teams exploring options.
- Initial setup for CRM integrations and the production studio involves a learning curve, particularly for smaller teams without dedicated marketing operations support.


**Pricing:** Custom pricing;[Request a demo](https://www.zuddl.com/pricing)


**Ratings:** 4.8/5 on G2 · 4.5/5 on Capterra


**Best for:** B2B demand generation teams running four or more webinars per month who need a single platform that handles broadcast, on-demand gating, CRM engagement sync, and content repurposing without requiring separate video editing or hosting tools.


### BigMarker


BigMarker supports live, simulive, automated, and on-demand webinars natively from one platform, with a wide range of native CRM and marketing automation integration connections. It fits mid-market to enterprise teams that need to run both free and paid webinar programs across multiple formats.


**What it does well**


- All four broadcast modes (live, simulive, automated/evergreen, on-demand) are native to the platform, giving teams format flexibility without switching tools.
- Native integrations span Salesforce, HubSpot, Marketo, Pardot, Eloqua, and ActiveCampaign, covering more CRM and MAP connections than most competitors in this list.
- Q&A with audience upvoting surfaces the most relevant questions during sessions, and moderated chat, polls, and handouts are available for attendee engagement.
- Embeddable webinar rooms and API widgets let teams host sessions on owned domains rather than redirecting attendees to a third-party URL.


**Where it has gaps**


- No evidence of one-click webinar cloning with inherited CRM mappings, email sequences, and branded assets.
- No AI-based content repurposing, clip generation, or branded on-demand content hub.
- Granular engagement signal sync (poll responses, CTA clicks, minutes watched flowing to CRM) is not documented in vendor materials.
- No pipeline attribution or revenue impact reporting.


**Pricing:** Custom pricing across three tiers (Webcast Basic, Professional, Enterprise). Contact sales for quotes.


**Ratings:** 4.7/5 on G2 · 4.8/5 on Capterra


**Best for:** Mid-market B2B teams running a mix of free lead-generation webinars and paid training or certification events who need broad native CRM coverage and the flexibility to embed sessions on their own site.


### Demio


Demio offers live, automated, and on-demand webinar capabilities with in-session CTAs (called "Featured Actions") designed to drive conversion during the presentation. It fits small to mid-size B2B marketing teams focused on webinar-driven demand generation with a need for attendee-level engagement analytics.


**What it does well**


- Featured Actions (embedded CTAs) appear during live and automated sessions, enabling mid-presentation conversion moments such as demo requests or resource downloads without disrupting the attendee experience.
- Detailed analytics track attendance, CTA clicks, poll engagement, handout downloads, and session timing at the individual attendee level, with an activity timeline for personalizing follow-up outreach.
- Automated webinar sequences replicate a live-feeling experience for evergreen campaigns, and on-demand replay pages transition from live registration with reduced manual effort.
- Showcase feature creates a branded collection page displaying upcoming and past events with customizable layout, colors, and fonts for a cohesive webinar program presence.


**Where it has gaps**


- Salesforce integration is described by reviewers as less mature than HubSpot.
- No native AI-based clip creation or content repurposing tools.
- Multi-webinar ROI comparison and pipeline attribution dashboards are not available natively.


**Pricing:** Starter from $45/month (annual) for 50 attendees. Growth from $80/month (annual) for 150 attendees. Premium from $2,354/year. Unlimited plan requires custom pricing.


**Ratings:** 4.6/5 on G2 · 4.7/5 on Capterra


**Best for:** B2B marketing teams running 2 to 8 webinars per month who prioritize in-session conversion tools and attendee-level engagement tracking over enterprise CRM sync depth or AI content repurposing.


### Livestorm


Livestorm is a browser-based webinar platform with native live and on-demand modes, GDPR compliance, and ISO 27001 certification. It serves B2B teams in regulated or security-conscious environments who need a compliant platform with straightforward setup.


**What it does well**


- Live-to-on-demand conversion is described as instant, turning live sessions into available on-demand recordings with evergreen registration pages and embeddable forms.
- Browser-based access with no download required reduces attendee friction and no-show rates, a feature consistently praised by reviewers on both G2 and Capterra.
- Multi-workspace support under one contract with unified billing and reporting gives larger organizations a way to manage multiple teams or business units from a single account.


**Where it has gaps**


- Simulive mode (pre-recorded content played at a scheduled time with live Q&A) is not confirmed in vendor materials. Teams running global webinar series across time zones may need presenters available live.
- CRM sync fidelity is unclear. Salesforce is named as a native integration, but whether granular engagement signals (poll responses, minutes watched, CTA clicks) pass through to CRM is not documented.
- No AI-based content repurposing, clip generation, or attendance heatmaps. A company page feature hosts past events but does not transform recordings into distributable content assets.
- Attendee-credit pricing model is cited by reviewers as difficult to predict at scale, with costs rising sharply as audience size grows.


**Pricing:** Free plan available (30 attendee credits/year, up to 30-minute sessions). Paid tier pricing requires contact.


**Ratings:** 4.4/5 on G2 · 4.7/5 on Capterra


**Best for:** B2B teams in GDPR-regulated industries that need a browser-based, ISO 27001-certified platform for live and on-demand webinars and can accommodate a compliance-first platform with less depth in simulive, content repurposing, and pipeline attribution.


### GoTo Webinar


GoTo Webinar provides live, simulive, and cloud-recorded webinar modes with published pricing tiers that scale up to 2,000 participants. It fits established B2B organizations with an existing GoTo ecosystem that need a reliable, familiar platform for recurring webinar programs.


**What it does well**


- Simulive events (automated, pre-recorded content played at a scheduled time) are a confirmed capability, supporting global teams that need to run sessions without live presenter availability.
- AI-generated transcripts and summaries are available post-event, giving teams a starting point for repurposing webinar content into written formats.
- Polls, Q&A, breakout rooms, and closed captioning are available during live sessions, with Q&A moderation tools praised by reviewers managing large audiences.


**Where it has gaps**


- CRM syncs are limited to registration and attendance status.
- No branded on-demand content hub. Recordings sit in an internal dashboard, and on-demand replay pages carry GoTo Webinar branding, creating brand inconsistency.
- Simulive mode lacks confirmed ability to layer live Q&A mid-broadcast.
- No pipeline attribution or revenue impact dashboard.


**Pricing:** Multiple published tiers (Lite, Standard, Enterprise, Flex). Free trial available.


**Ratings:** 4.2/5 on G2 · 4.5/5 on Capterra


**Best for:** B2B teams already in the GoTo ecosystem who run monthly webinars at 500 to 2,000 attendee scale and need reliable simulive with AI transcripts, but do not require deep CRM engagement sync or content repurposing tools.


### WebinarGeek


WebinarGeek supports live, automated, and on-demand webinar types natively from a browser-based platform with GDPR compliance and EU data storage. It fits European B2B teams and SMBs that need a straightforward platform with payment gating for monetized webinar content.


**What it does well**


- Automated webinars support preloaded polls, quizzes, and CTA buttons with live chat enabled, replicating a live-feeling experience for evergreen campaigns without requiring presenter involvement.
- On-demand webinars are available 24/7 for self-paced viewer access, and a webinar channel page displays all upcoming and on-demand webinars in a single hub.
- Paid webinar capability with Stripe or Mollie payment processing enables monetized on-demand content distribution.


**Where it has gaps**


- Native bi-directional CRM sync is not available.
- No content clipping or repurposing tools.
- Branding customization is described as surface-level by reviewers, with limitations on custom colors, fonts, and email sender identity at lower tiers.
- Analytics stop at attendance counts and poll results, with no pipeline attribution, revenue tracking, or attendee-level engagement profiles for sales.


**Pricing:** Basic €49/month (up to 50 viewers); Premium €69/month (up to 1,000 viewers); Enterprise €349/month (up to 5,000 viewers). 14-day free trial available.


**Ratings:** 4.5/5 on G2 · 4.6/5 on Capterra


**Best for:** European SMB marketing teams running automated and on-demand webinar programs at moderate scale who need GDPR-compliant hosting with payment gating and can work without deep CRM sync or content repurposing.


### ClickMeeting


ClickMeeting runs live, automated, and on-demand webinars natively with a visual timeline editor for configuring when polls, CTAs, and chat messages appear during automated sessions. It fits SMB and mid-market teams running recurring training, product demos, or sales webinars.


**What it does well**


- The visual timeline editor for automated webinars lets organizers schedule when polls, CTAs, chat messages, and video segments fire during a pre-recorded session, reducing the manual coordination typically required for simulive-style broadcasts.
- Live, automated, and on-demand modes are available within a single account, and the webinar cycle automation handles pre-event reminders, recording publication, follow-ups, and attendee redirects.
- White-label options on the Enterprise plan allow full removal of ClickMeeting branding, and custom-branded event landing pages are available across all tiers.


**Where it has gaps**


- No native Salesforce integration.
- One-click cloning of webinars with all settings intact (forms, email sequences, CRM mappings) is not confirmed.
- No AI-based content repurposing, branded content hub, or attendance heatmaps.
- Pipeline attribution and revenue reporting are absent.


**Pricing:** Live from $32/month (25 attendees); Automated from $48/month (25 attendees); Enterprise custom pricing. 14-day free trial.


**Ratings:** 4.2/5 on G2 · 4.5/5 on Capterra


**Best for:** SMB teams running weekly sales demos or training webinars who want a simple automated scheduling cycle with visual timeline control and do not require Salesforce integration or post-event content repurposing.


### LiveWebinar


LiveWebinar is a browser-based platform with live webinar delivery, on-demand recording capability, and interactive tools including breakout rooms and whiteboards. It fits teams running workshop-style or training webinars that need collaborative in-session features at an accessible price point.


**What it does well**


- In-session engagement tools include polls, surveys, interactive whiteboards, breakout rooms, and chat, making it well-suited for training and workshop formats that require collaboration beyond passive viewing.
- Browser-based access across all devices (browsers, smart TVs, mobile, conferencing systems) removes download friction for both organizers and attendees.
- Recordings can be stored on Amazon S3 or FTP servers, giving technical teams flexibility in managing recording infrastructure and compliance requirements.


**Where it has gaps**


- True simulive mode (pre-recorded content played at a scheduled time with live Q&A overlay) is not confirmed in vendor materials.
- CRM sync is limited to registration and attendance status via Zapier. No native Salesforce campaign hierarchy mapping.
- No AI-based content repurposing, branded on-demand content hub, or attendance heatmaps.
- Each webinar setup requires manual reconfiguration of forms and settings. No one-click cloning or template inheritance for high-volume series.


**Pricing:** Free plan available. PRO from $32/month (25 to 100 attendees); Business Plus from $42/month (up to 500 attendees); Premium from $62/month (up to 1,000 attendees). Enterprise pricing via quote.


**Ratings:** 4.4/5 on G2 · 4.7/5 on Capterra


**Best for:** Training and enablement teams running interactive workshop-format webinars with breakout rooms and whiteboards who need a budget-friendly, browser-based platform and can manage CRM sync and content distribution externally.


### Riverside


Riverside captures 4K video and uncompressed audio locally on each participant's device, with live, pre-recorded simulive, and on-demand webinar modes plus editing tools that generate social clips, transcriptions, and highlight reels. It fits content and media teams that need broadcast-quality recordings and post-webinar repurposing alongside standard webinar delivery.


**What it does well**


- 4K local recording on each participant's device produces broadcast-quality output that is resilient to internet instability, giving teams that repurpose webinar content heavily a recording foundation few competitors in this list match.
- Pre-recorded webinars can be scheduled and streamed at a set time with live chat, polls, and Q&A active during playback, functioning as a simulive mode. On-demand viewing is also available for viewers to watch at any time.
- Magic Clips automatically generate short social-ready snippets from full recordings, and text-based editing lets teams cut video by editing the transcript rather than scrubbing a timeline.
- Live call-ins allow audience members to join as speakers during a webinar, adding a layer of interactivity beyond standard Q&A and polls.
- Automated reminder emails before events and follow-up emails after events support lead nurturing workflows from within the platform.


**Where it has gaps**


- CRM integrations (HubSpot, Salesforce, Marketo) are listed for registration data, but sync fidelity for engagement signals (poll responses, CTA clicks, minutes watched) is not verified.
- Registration gating for on-demand replays is not confirmed in vendor materials.
- No one-click webinar cloning with inherited settings, branded on-demand content hub, or pipeline attribution dashboards.
- The Webinar plan caps registrants at 100. Business plan extends to 10,000.


**Pricing:** Free plan ($0, 2 hrs recording, 720p, watermarked); Pro $24/month (annual); Grow $34/month (annual); Webinar $79/month (annual, up to 100 registrants); Business custom pricing.


**Ratings:** 4.8/5 on G2 · 4.8/5 on Capterra


**Best for:** Content marketing teams that run webinars primarily to generate social clips, podcast episodes, and video assets, and who handle lead capture and CRM workflows through separate tools rather than expecting the webinar platform to manage the full funnel.


### WebinarKit


WebinarKit runs automated, evergreen, like-live, just-in-time, and instant-watch webinars with AI-driven chat that handles objections and drives conversions during automated sessions. It fits solopreneurs and individual marketers building always-on webinar funnels at a flat cost.


**What it does well**


- AI-driven automated chat engages viewers and handles objections during automated sessions without requiring a live moderator, with timed CTA overlays appearing at key moments to drive conversion.
- Unlimited webinars and attendees at the plan level remove per-event cost friction for high-volume evergreen programs.
- The funnel builder packages registration, thank-you, and replay pages together, reducing multi-step setup for each new automated webinar.


**Where it has gaps**


- No native Salesforce or HubSpot integration.
- No branded on-demand content library, AI clip generation, or attendance heatmaps.
- Live webinar engagement tools (Q&A moderation, breakout rooms) are limited compared to live-first platforms.
- Pipeline attribution, multi-webinar ROI comparison, and executive-facing reporting are not available.


**Pricing:** Lifetime deals from $497 one-time; monthly subscription from $79/month (unlimited webinars, automated + live). $1 for 7-day trial.


**Ratings:** 4.7/5 on G2 · Not available on Capterra


**Best for:** Solo marketers and coaches running high-volume evergreen webinar funnels who want AI-driven automated chat and unlimited webinars without per-event fees, and who manage CRM and analytics outside the webinar platform.


### EverWebinar


EverWebinar runs automated webinars exclusively, with chat simulation, timed offers, and just-in-time scheduling that give pre-recorded sessions a live-feeling experience. It fits individual marketers running set-and-forget automated sequences for lead generation or course promotion.


**What it does well**


- Chat simulation at specific timestamps during automated playback creates the appearance of live interaction, and timed offers (CTAs) display during the presentation to drive conversion at peak attention moments.
- Just-in-time scheduling lets registrants start watching almost immediately, functioning as an always-on gated lead capture asset.
- Hybrid mode plays pre-recorded video with live chat capability, letting organizers add a layer of real-time interaction without delivering the full presentation live.


**Where it has gaps**


- No live webinar mode.
- No native CRM integration with Salesforce or HubSpot.
- No content repurposing, branded on-demand library, or AI clip generation.
- Branding and customization options are limited.


**Pricing:** Starting at $99/month (billed annually). $1 trial for 14 days.


**Ratings:** 3.9/5 on G2 · 3.9/5 on Capterra


**Best for:** Individual marketers or course creators who need a dedicated automated webinar tool with timed offers and chat simulation, and who do not require live broadcast capability, CRM engagement sync, or content repurposing.


### Webinar.net


Webinar.net supports live, pre-recorded rebroadcast, and on-demand webinars with automatic conversion from live to on-demand after the event. It emphasizes fast setup, browser-based delivery, and branded registration pages, fitting teams that need a straightforward platform with built-in on-demand conversion.


**What it does well**


- Any live webinar automatically converts into an on-demand webinar after the session ends, removing manual steps to make recordings available for post-event viewing.
- Pre-recorded live webinars can be rebroadcast repeatedly with audience interaction, allowing teams to re-run high-performing sessions without presenters going live again.
- Scheduling and launching a live webinar is fast, with the vendor claiming setup in under 60 seconds and reviewers confirming minimal ramp time for new team members.
- Browser-based delivery with no plugins required reduces attendee friction and technical support requests during sessions.
- Engagement tools include live polling with real-time results, moderated Q&A, one-to-one attendee-presenter messaging, document sharing, and post-webinar surveys.


**Where it has gaps**


- No CRM integrations documented on vendor pages.
- No native content repurposing, branded content hub, or AI clip generation.
- Analytics are described as limited by reviewers, who want more granular per-attendee engagement breakdowns and cannot access pipeline attribution within the platform.
- Custom post-registration pages are available, but gating controls for on-demand replays are not detailed.


**Pricing:** Starting from approximately $500/month (up to 100 live attendees). Enterprise from $1,250/month. Free trial available.


**Ratings:** 4.7/5 on G2 · Not available on Capterra


**Best for:** Teams running a small number of live-only webinars per quarter who need fast setup and do not require simulive, CRM integration, content repurposing, or program-level analytics.


### Webinar+


Webinar+ (a Brandlive product) delivers cinematic, high-production webinar experiences with live, pre-recorded, and on-demand session types, plus managed production services including presenter coaching, technical rehearsals, and day-of event management. It fits organizations that need broadcast-quality production for high-stakes webinar events with on-demand replay.


**What it does well**


- Cinematic layouts, branded intros, lower thirds, and transitions give webinar sessions a production quality that approaches broadcast television, differentiating them from standard screen-share formats.
- On-demand is available as a native session type alongside live and pre-recorded broadcasts, allowing teams to offer post-event viewing without third-party hosting.
- Managed production services handle planning, scheduling, technical rehearsals, presenter coaching, and day-of management, reducing the operational burden on internal marketing teams for flagship events.
- Scale claims support up to 1,000,000 concurrent attendees, positioning the platform for large-audience broadcasts.


**Where it has gaps**


- CRM integration depth is not documented beyond general "connect engagement data across systems" claims.
- Program-level cloning, template inheritance, and one-click webinar duplication are not evidenced.
- No AI-based content repurposing outputs (clips, blog drafts, social posts) or branded on-demand hub confirmed at feature level.
- Pipeline attribution dashboards, multi-webinar ROI comparison, and attendee-level engagement profiles for sales are not confirmed in vendor materials.


**Pricing:** Custom pricing; not listed publicly.


**Ratings:** Not available on G2 · Not available on Capterra


**Best for:** Enterprise organizations running quarterly or annual flagship webinars where production quality is the primary differentiator and the team needs managed services support rather than self-serve program scalability.


## What to look for in on-demand webinar platforms for B2B event teams


**Broadcast mode flexibility:** Evaluate whether the platform supports live, simulive, and on-demand natively within one workflow. Teams that cannot run simulive force speakers to present multiple times across time zones, and platforms without automated on-demand delay post-event lead capture.


**CRM integration and engagement data sync:** Check whether the sync passes granular signals (poll responses, CTA clicks, minutes watched) or only registration and attendance status. Platforms that sync only binary attended/not-attended data leave sales reps without differentiation signals for outreach.


**Post-webinar content hub and repurposing:** Determine whether recordings are transformed into clips, social posts, and searchable libraries within the platform, or require manual export to third-party editors. Teams without in-platform repurposing typically spend 8 or more hours per webinar on manual editing and lose ongoing pipeline from undistributed content.


**Webinar program scalability and cloning:** Test whether the second webinar in a series inherits forms, CRM mappings,[email sequences](https://www.zuddl.com/platform/event-registration-and-ticketing-software/event-communications) , and branded assets from the first. Platforms that require manual rebuilding per event introduce configuration drift and consume capacity at four or more webinars per month.


**Brand control across every touchpoint:** Assess brand coverage across the full attendee journey:[registration pages](https://www.zuddl.com/platform/event-registration-and-ticketing-software/branding-events) , emails, in-webinar studio, and on-demand replay hub. Platforms that brand only the registration page but default to generic in-room and replay experiences create visible brand discontinuity for attendees.


**On-demand access control and gating:** Verify whether the platform supports gated (form fill), ungated (public), and private link sharing for on-demand content. Teams that cannot gate replays lose the ability to use on-demand webinars as ongoing lead generation assets.


**In-webinar engagement and live conversion:** Look for individual-level capture of poll responses, Q&A activity, and CTA clicks that flow into CRM. Platforms that only report aggregate attendance produce a binary signal insufficient for lead scoring. If you're building surveys to[help your webinar program drive business decisions](https://17-post-webinar-survey-questions-to-help-you-drive-decisions/) , check out the linked guide.


**Pipeline attribution and ROI reporting:** Confirm whether the platform connects webinar engagement to pipeline influenced and revenue generated. Teams that cannot attribute pipeline to specific webinars cannot defend program investment at budget review.


## Questions people ask about on-demand webinar platforms


**What is the difference between automated webinars and on-demand webinars?**


Automated webinars play pre-recorded content at a scheduled time, simulating a live broadcast with timed polls, chat, and CTAs. On-demand webinars let viewers access the recording at any time on their own schedule. Some platforms, such as Zuddl, BigMarker, and Demio, support both modes natively. Automated sessions create urgency through scheduled start times. On-demand removes scheduling friction entirely.


**What features should an on-demand webinar platform have?**


At minimum: gated and ungated access controls for replays, automated transition from live registration to on-demand page, CRM sync that passes engagement signals (not just attendance), and a branded replay experience. Platforms that also offer AI content repurposing and attendance heatmaps extend the webinar's pipeline-generating lifespan well beyond the live date.


**Can automated webinars include interactive features like chat and polls?**


Yes. WebinarKit and EverWebinar support chat simulation and timed polls during automated playback. Demio and ClickMeeting enable preloaded polls and CTAs during automated sessions. Zuddl supports real-time polls, Q&A, and embedded CTAs during simulive sessions with live interaction capability. The depth of individual-level engagement data capture varies significantly across these platforms.


**What integrations do on-demand webinar platforms support?**


Most platforms integrate with HubSpot and Zapier. Fewer offer native Salesforce bi-directional sync with granular engagement data. Zuddl, BigMarker, and Demio name Salesforce, HubSpot, and Marketo as native integrations. The critical question is what data passes through: registration status only, or engagement signals like poll responses, CTA clicks, and minutes watched.
